facts.text: Two NIOSH studies published in Mining, Metallurgy & Exploration in 2019 examined how stop-capable proximity detection systems on mobile haulage machines were received in underground coal mining.
facts.quote: Two NIOSH studies published in Mining, Metallurgy & Exploration in 2019 describe how stop-capable proximity detection systems (PDS) on mobile haulage machines were received:

facts.text: Interviews by Bellanca, Helton, McNinch and Swanson with mineworkers at seven underground coal mines found that mobile proximity detection systems unnecessarily shut down vehicles from once a day to 15 times during a single cut of coal.
facts.quote: Interviews with mineworkers at seven underground coal mines (Bellanca, Helton, McNinch and Swanson) found that mobile PDSs "unnecessarily shut down vehicles anywhere from once a day up to 15 times during a single cut of coal"

facts.text: In interviews with mineworkers at seven underground coal mines, over 80% of workers said mobile proximity detection systems made work more difficult.
facts.quote: over 80% of workers said the systems made work more difficult

facts.text: In interviews with mineworkers at seven underground coal mines, nearly 70% of workers were concerned about how and when mobile proximity detection systems take control.
facts.quote: nearly 70% were concerned about "how and when the mobile PDS takes control"

facts.text: Mineworkers interviewed at seven underground coal mines reported frustration from nuisance trips and interference caused by mobile proximity detection systems.
facts.quote: workers reported frustration from "nuisance trips and interference" [11]. **Independent**.

facts.text: A task-technology-fit study by Swanson and Bellanca with leaders at two coal mines rated mobile proximity detection systems favorably on training and ease of use, system feedback, user authorization and experience.
facts.quote: A task-technology-fit study with leaders at two coal mines (Swanson and Bellanca) rated mobile PDS favorably on training and ease of use, system feedback, user authorization and experience

facts.text: The task-technology-fit study by Swanson and Bellanca with leaders at two coal mines rated mobile proximity detection systems less favorably on safety, compatibility, task completion and reliability.
facts.quote: but less favorably on safety, compatibility, task completion and reliability

facts.text: The task-technology-fit study with leaders at two coal mines found that loading, troubleshooting, maintenance and inspections could become more difficult with mobile proximity detection systems.
facts.quote: loading, troubleshooting, maintenance and inspections could become more difficult

facts.text: Leaders at two coal mines specifically raised false alarms and compatibility problems in the task-technology-fit study of mobile proximity detection systems.
facts.quote: false alarms and compatibility problems were raised specifically.

facts.text: The Swanson and Bellanca study discusses a June 2017 fatal accident involving an underground continuous-miner operator who had disabled the machine's protection; the case involved a wearable proximity detection system, not a surface haul-truck warning system.
facts.quote: The same study discusses a June 2017 fatal accident in which a continuous-miner operator had disabled the machine's protection

facts.text: The investigation of the June 2017 fatal continuous-miner accident found that emergency-stop override had become common practice at the underground coal mine.
facts.quote: the investigation found that emergency-stop override had become common practice at that mine

facts.text: The investigation of the June 2017 fatal continuous-miner accident recorded 87 prior activations of the deceased worker's emergency-stop override.
facts.quote: recorded 87 prior activations of the deceased worker's override [12].

facts.text: The underground continuous-miner and wearable proximity detection system case shows why bypass resistance and task compatibility belong in the safety case for automatic braking, although the case is not about a surface haul-truck warning system.
facts.quote: This involves a continuous miner and wearable PDS underground, not a surface haul-truck warning system, but it shows why bypass resistance and task compatibility belong in the safety case for automatic braking.
